stories.headline: Etched Closes $300 Million Series C at $10.3 Billion to Challenge Nvidia on Inference
stories.key_takeaway: Etched raised a $300M Series C at a $10.3B valuation, doubling in seven months, to scale its transformer-only Sohu inference chips as a direct economic challenge to Nvidia's general-purpose GPUs.

pull_quote.text: These are all people who actually tried the hardware and are very excited about it.

stories.article_excerpt: Four years ago, three Harvard undergraduates dropped out of school on a wager most of Silicon Valley thought was reckless.

stories.headline: AegisAI Raises $36 Million to Fight AI-Generated Phishing at the Inbox
stories.key_takeaway: AegisAI's $36M Series A shows AI funding chasing AI's own fallout: cheap, flawless AI-written phishing now demands language- and intent-aware defense that legacy scanners cannot deliver.

pull_quote.text: You cannot patch human trust. When the attack is AI, the defense has to be AI.

stories.article_excerpt: The same generative AI that lets a marketer draft a flawless cold email now lets a criminal write a flawless con.

stories.headline: Paper Raises $34 Million to Become the Design Layer for AI-Built Software
stories.key_takeaway: Paper raised a $34M Series A led by Accel and ICONIQ to build an HTML/CSS-based design canvas positioned to collapse the design-to-engineering handoff in an era of AI coding agents.

pull_quote.text: Most design tools were built for a world where humans did all the work. Paper is built for a world where humans and AI create together.

stories.article_excerpt: When software gets written by machines, who draws the picture first? A startup called Paper is betting on the answer.

stories.headline: Ropedia Raises $30 Million to Build the Data Layer for Physical AI
stories.key_takeaway: Ropedia raised $30M in pre-A funding to scale its wearable-driven pipeline that turns real human interaction data into training fuel for robots, betting that data curation is the true bottleneck for physical AI.

pull_quote.text: There's not yet going to be a massive deployment of robots. We need to unlock the ChatGPT moment for robotics first.

stories.article_excerpt: Singapore-based Ropedia has raised $30 million to scale a bet on what the next great leap in robotics really needs.

stories.headline: Elio Raises $21 Million to Build Sensors Made for Machines, Not Human Eyes
stories.key_takeaway: Elio raised $21M to build AI-native sensors that put computation inside the optics so machines, not human eyes, decide what light to capture.

pull_quote.text: Sensing starts to behave like software: the same unit gets more capable over time, instead of becoming outdated.

stories.article_excerpt: For a century, the camera has been designed around a single customer: the human eye. Elio wants to change that.

stories.headline: Black Forest Labs' FLUX 3 Folds Image, Video, Audio and Robot Control Into One Model
stories.key_takeaway: Black Forest Labs' FLUX 3 unifies image, video, audio and robot action prediction in one architecture, and its FLUX-mimic model is already running robots on a factory floor, marking the lab's decisive move into physical AI.

pull_quote.text: The process of predicting video is the process of learning principles of the real physical world such as weight, contact and timing.
pull_quote.role: Co-founder and CEO, Black Forest Labs

stories.article_excerpt: The German lab that taught the internet to generate photorealistic images now wants to teach machines to move.

stories.headline: Genspark's 'AI Workspace 6.0' Adds a Perpetual Memory and Its First Hardware
stories.key_takeaway: Genspark's AI Workspace 6.0 pairs SecondBrain, a persistent cross-app memory layer for AI agents, with SecondBrain Note, a card-sized recorder that is the company's first hardware, betting that context, not model size, wins the agent era.

pull_quote.text: Today, using AI is like collaborating with a genius who has a goldfish memory.

stories.article_excerpt: For two years, the pitch behind the AI agent boom has run into the same wall: the agent forgets what you told it.

stories.headline: OpenAI's Codex Doubles to 10 Million Users and Learns to Take Voice Commands
stories.key_takeaway: OpenAI's Codex and ChatGPT Work agents together doubled to 10 million weekly users while gaining full-duplex voice control that can be operated remotely from a phone.

pull_quote.text: ChatGPT Voice is now in the desktop app. Control your computer and direct multiple agents running in ChatGPT Work or Codex, using just your voice.

stories.article_excerpt: OpenAI's coding agent is no longer a niche tool for early adopters tinkering at a keyboard.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang Makes His X Debut With a Manifesto for Open AI Models
stories.key_takeaway: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang broke his silence on X to publish a letter arguing open AI models are essential to safety, innovation and sovereignty, framing openness as an American strength just as Chinese open-weight models surge.

pull_quote.text: The world needs both frontier closed models and frontier open models.

stories.article_excerpt: Jensen Huang has run Nvidia for more than three decades. This week he finally started posting on X.

stories.headline: A New Open-Source Framework Lets AI Move Between Robot Bodies
stories.key_takeaway: CMU-led researchers released RIO, an open-source framework that gives AI models and robot software a unified, modular interface so they can move between arms, humanoids and other hardware without rewriting the control stack.

pull_quote.text: The biggest bottleneck in robot learning research isn't ideas, it is infrastructure.
pull_quote.role: Associate Research Professor, Carnegie Mellon University

stories.article_excerpt: Getting a new robot to do anything at all can eat a semester before a student tests a single idea.

stories.headline: COMPASS Tackles the Long-Horizon Problem That Trips Up AI Agents
stories.key_takeaway: COMPASS reframes long-horizon agent failure as a context-management problem, using a three-part architecture that separates execution, strategic oversight and evolving context summaries to keep agents coherent over extended multi-step tasks.

pull_quote.text: Extended histories cause agents to overlook critical evidence or become distracted by irrelevant information, leaving them unable to replan effectively or reflect on earlier mistakes.

stories.article_excerpt: Ask a model to answer a question and it does fine. Ask it to run a 40-step research task and it drifts.

stories.headline: Teaching AI Agents to Plan Before They Act, Efficiently
stories.key_takeaway: A CMU-linked paper trains agents to self-regulate how much they plan, cutting reasoning tokens by up to roughly 95% while matching or beating far larger models on accuracy.

pull_quote.text: RL increases average planning horizon by 22.8% while planning frequency grows only 2.0%, indicating that the model learns to plan further ahead rather than more often.

stories.article_excerpt: The reigning recipe for smarter AI agents in 2026 has been blunt: let them think longer. This paper pushes back.

stories.headline: Publishers and Authors Sue Google, Alleging Gemini Was Trained on Stripped-Down Books
stories.key_takeaway: Major publishers and author Scott Turow are suing Google over Gemini training, and their standout claim is not fair use but that Google illegally stripped copyright-management information from books to hide the infringement under DMCA Section 1202.

pull_quote.text: Google illegally copied works from all these scope-limited programs for AI training, knowing it lacked authorization to do so.

stories.article_excerpt: Three of the world's largest publishers and a best-known novelist accuse Google of building Gemini on stolen books.

stories.headline: Researchers Say a Booby-Trapped Repo Can Make Claude Code Leak Files Silently
stories.key_takeaway: Tego AI says a rigged repo's CLAUDE.md symlink import can make Claude Code silently exfiltrate an out-of-project file on its first request, while Anthropic says the behavior falls within the tool's documented 'trust this folder' threat model.

pull_quote.text: Clone a repo, answer the same 'trust this folder?' question you always answer, and a file from outside that repo can leave your machine on the first request.

stories.article_excerpt: A security firm says an ordinary-looking repository can be rigged to make Claude Code read and leak a secret file.

stories.headline: FTC Weighs a Policy Targeting AI Systems That Suppress Accuracy
stories.key_takeaway: The FTC proposed applying its Section 5 deception authority to AI companies that market systems as accurate and objective while secretly steering outputs, with public comments due July 31, 2026.

pull_quote.text: The FTC wants to hear from businesses and consumers about their experiences and concerns regarding the subversion of AI systems for ideological ends.

stories.article_excerpt: The FTC has put AI companies on notice that quietly tuning a chatbot's outputs could be an unfair or deceptive practice.
